title: My first time seeing Oliver! the musical | London Theatre Review 2025
transcript: everyone knows the story of Oliver Twist but what if I told you that I have never seen this musical until I went to check out the latest production that just opened in the West End in this video I'm going to share my thoughts with you and why you should go and check out this musical have you seen Oliver let me know in the comments below welcome to my channel my name is Christina and I'm here to help you have the best London theater experience by sharing my reviews cheap ticket deals and London insights if this sounds like a little bit of you then make sure to like And subscribe Oliver the musical is based on a novel by Charles Dickens Oliver Twist not many writers and novelists have such a special place in London's heart as Charles Dickens because he did live and breathe this city both good and bad and in Victorian London in England there was way more bad than good to talk about so this is not a happy story the story follows Oliver who is an abandoned orphan and he's left at this workhouse and one day when he asked for more food they decided to sell him because he was not an obedient child and from here the plot starts he's first sold to this couple who are running a funeral shop and that is the first time when Oliver is faced with completely being on his own and he decides to run away from it and while running away he meets Artful Dodger who is a thief and this way he joins this gang of boys who are Street thieves and from here his Adventures Continue all the way up until the end where a different plot continues but I'm not going to spoil it for you if you're not aware of this which I doubt but let's keep keep it a secret so Oliver is a bleak story set in a very difficult time in London so why do people love it so much where there is a lot of Hope kindness and just general upbeat Vibe which is mainly due to music and this is kind of what solidify this as a classic of musical theater let's talk about the music the music is written by Lionel Bart who has written this in 1960 when this musical premiered for the first time and ever since it's been a massive commercial success and it's gone on to perform all over the world including Broadway in many different countries around the world and the best part about this musical is that it is not said at all there are maybe a couple of heartfelt ballads but overall it's a very upbeat and seemingly happy show with a lot of Happy Tunes and catching numbers they will literally make you dance in your seat so how is this possible when the story is so sad as I mentioned well Lionel has leaned into some general themes of love and hardship and Community I think that this show has a lot of people coming together I think even in the workhouse there is a community of children and then there is a community of Guardians and then when Oliver becomes a thief there is a community of Thieves and I think when there is a big community of people it is inevitable to have a big belter of a song that is just a big number and it's really nice to see it on stage the song that gave me goosebumps is definitely where is love which is a song that Oliver sings when he's left alone for the first night and in this place where he was sold to and he needs to sleep in a coffin and he sings this song asking where is This Love that everyone is talking about where is the Hope and does he actually deserve it and it is such a beautiful moment especially because Oliver is played by a really young actor normally between ages of 9 to 11 and their voices are so soft and beautiful and in this case I've seen Ken Eagle service who delivered this song spectacularly like I really felt like crying and being so emotional at the same time of how beautiful that moment in the show was especially because what precedes that number is quite a few upbeat songs and then after it it also goes straight into something that is a bit more catchy and is entertaining to watch so I think this is a perfect way to break those two very hectic narratives that happen around Oliver also Food Glorious Food is one of the most beloved Classics that everyone enjoys because it's one of those opening number that loves you in straight away it showcases the action of the musical from the get-go and you are hooked so it was fantastic seeing that on stage probably the biggest and most emotional ballad in the show apart from where his love is as long as he needs me sang by ncy who delivers this is a heart-felt ballad for loving a man who is ultimately not good for her and it was one of those numbers that got a massive standing ofation consider yourself is another number that is absolutely delightful to watch on stage especially in this production the character of Artful Dodger is shining through this number and it is such a fun and amusing way to see friendship develop on stage and this is all held with amazing sets and costume design and different choreographies that really helped this number come to life and the reason why all these numbers managed to shine through is because of the great cast that this production has assembled the day I went to see the show Oliver was played by Ken Eagle service and he is an absolute Delight to watch such a confident performance from such a little human and such a big actor I was so impressed by him but also you should be aware that there are four Olivers who are in the principal cast and they alternate so you might see someone else but I'm sure that they will be brilliant this is an incredible role for such young actors to portray on stage so it's always spectacular seeing them how they find their feet and how confident they are on stage another fantastic young actor delivered the role of Artful Dodger Billy Jenkins you might know him from pey blinders or Le Miser where he played gav he's playing the role with a lot of cheekiness but also genuine love and care for all of it Chen Holmes is in the role of ncy and she's nothing short of spectacular some of the biggest numbers in the show are ones that she's singing and every time that she's on stage you really feel it there's such Poise and presence that she brings and she was such a joy to watch definitely the most talked about performance in this production is by Simon Lipkin who is portraying the role of Fagan Fagan is a character who gathers orphan children and teaches them how to pick pockets so he's kind of the leader of this little criminal group and he's kind of exploiting children but I think in this production there is a lot of playfulness to this character and also a lot of care that Fagan is delivered with and he's almost this kind of kid himself and a dreamer who is just trying to help out these unfortunate children but Simon has delivered such an incredible performance adding a lot of nuance to this character and also a lot of playfulness so some of his numbers were the most exciting to watch Ever since this musical premiered in 1960s there's always been a desire to bring the world of Oliver Twist to stage with an elaborate set design and this production is no different located in a city and with a quite a lot of different set changes because they're quite a lot of environments that Oliver is going through it is really hard to do that if the set doesn't really allow for these changes and I'm pleased to tell you that the set in the latest production of Oliver is great there are quite a few elements that are coming in and out depending on the set there's also middle part of the stage that is revolving this really helps convey this feeling of Oliver truly running away from something and there are also some interesting elements of how London is brought to life through different buildings and bridges so overall there's a lot of movement on stage in terms of the set design which really helps you be on board with this story there are also some projections on the stage especially the beginning and the opening scene that's when they come to light the moves but also the closing scene has a really nice projection at the back so this set design really delivers on the promise of taking you to Victorian London another thing that makes this production of Oliver very special is the duo of Cameron McIntosh who is a producer and Matthew Bourne who is a choreographer and director in this case as well working together on Oliver again they worked on Oliver together her in 1994 and now almost 30 years later they're bringing a new version for fresh audiences to tell this story that a lot of people have close in their heart so when it comes to choreography Matthew Bourne is one of those people who is the name that everyone knows in the world of theater that when you see his name you know that the production has a lot of credibility behind it especially when it comes to choreography but there's just this feeling of both of them being very comfortable with this show and just delivering what they know the best and that is the essence of the show in various different ways so with these two people attached to this production you know that this is a show that has been handled with a lot of care and attention to detail and also with a lot of love cuz there's a lot of history behind this show especially when it comes to these two giants of theater working together so my overall opinion on Oliver the musical as a person who has never seen it before is that it is a mustsee just from the perspective of being such a classic of musical theater and such an important piece of British history so if you're in for something that will really bring this to elements to life then this is the perfect musical to check out is this the best show that I have seen in the western probably not would I go and see it again again I don't think so I think it's one of those shows that I will definitely listen to soundtrack of every now and then but I don't think that this is my favorite musical ever but I think if you have a connection from knowing this show from before and you love the story then seeing this on stage is going to be so amazing also this is a perfect show to take your kids to because there is also a lot of kids in the cast so it's a perfect watch for the whole family and I think if it's just for that then it's totally worth exploring it especially throughout whole 2025 because this show has just opened is set to continue performing for a long long time if you're not 100% sold on seeing Oliver then I'm pleased to tell you that there are a few more shows that I really enjoyed in 2024 which you can still see in 2025 so check out this video
